title: Special Order Spending and the Refund Allowance Multiplier — Ridgeline Consumer Credit Training Note
content:
**What the multiplier is.** On a return credit to a Ridgeline Consumer Credit account, the late-posting allowance is multiplied by an allowance multiplier set by the account's own purchases made through special orders — purchases charged to the account through Ridgeline Special Order Services — in the last 12 months (dated less than 12 full months before today).

| Special order purchases on the account in the last 12 months | Allowance multiplier |
|---|---|
| total 5000.00 or more | 2 |
| total 1500.00 or more but less than 5000.00 | 1.5 |
| total less than 1500.00 | 1 |

**How it acts.** The late-posting allowance — its interest part together with any amount added to it — is multiplied by the allowance multiplier and the product is rounded to the nearest cent. The multiplier acts on the allowance only, never on the uncredited refund.

## Questions a new representative asks

**Which purchases count?** The posted purchase lines on this account whose purchase channel is special order, dated within the 12 months. Purchases through any other channel do not count.

**A customer's special order purchases total exactly 1500.00. Which multiplier applies?** 1.5. At 1499.99 it is 1; at 4999.99 it is 1.5; at 5000.00 it is 2.

**Hypothetical:** an allowance of 24.86 before the multiplier becomes 37.29 at 1.5 and 49.72 at 2.
